summary: Kasongo-Lunda territory in southern Kwango province borders Angola along the Kwango river and lies far from the eastern DRC conflict zones and south-east of the Mobondo militia theatre (Kwamouth, Bagata, northern Kwango/Kenge). No armed group is known to hold territory in the territory. The territorial seat Kasongo-Lunda and the main centres (Panzi, Tembo, Wamba Luadi, Pelende) are under ordinary state authority with the PNC as the main permanent force, alongside FARDC/border units on the Angolan frontier and customary chiefs. Rural villages are assessed as state-held by default with low confidence. Web research was unavailable for this run (search budget exhausted, search engines blocked), so all zones rest on default state presence.

zones.evidence: No armed group is known to control villages in Kasongo-Lunda territory; state authority is exercised through PNC posts, the territorial administration and customary chiefs. Border villages along the Kwango may see artisanal diamond-mining frictions and cross-border movements with Angola, but no lasting armed-group or foreign control is known.
